ledger.contains: IMF Country Report 13/32 (Comoros 2012 Article IV and fourth ECF review, Feb 2013; HTML, about 11,400 lines incl. tables, Fund relations, DSA, letter of intent, MEFP and TMU). Programme content: the footnote repeated under most tables that 2011-12 revenue includes ECP receipts of about 3% of GDP a year; Text Figure 1 note (2012 about 3%); para 8 and MEFP para 3 on 2012 (ECP receipts projected at 4.5% of GDP against a 1.4% programme target, windfall 3.1%, 1.8% saved, 1% to transport infrastructure and malaria/HIV, 0.2% short-term loan to the oil importer); para 12 (4% in 2011-12, return to about 2% in 2013); the ECP feeding the narrowing of the current account deficit (no ECP number); TMU footnote defining the ECP (2008, KMF 1 million, about US$3,000, receipts routed via the Banque de France). The fiscal tables have no separate ECP line (it sits inside nontax revenue), so no KMF amounts. The 3%, 4%, 4.5%, 1.4%, 2% rows and the KMF 1 million term were already in the data; the windfall, savings and allocation figures are added (one new indicator proposed: cbi_revenue_saved_pct_gdp). The rest of the report (growth, inflation, debt, reserves, structural reforms) is out of scope. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

TSE compilation (171 pp.) of the 2012 Reglamento de Extranjería: definitions (investor: own capital in activities of economic and social interest), general fees and guarantee deposit, requirements for each temporary and permanent residence and special category (pensioners, rentistas, investors, workers, students, etc.), documentation and renewal. In scope: investor articles 87-93 (US$200,000 minimum in real estate, registrable goods, shares, securities, productive or national-interest projects; US$50 application fee; documents by investment type; forestry route with US$100,000 initial investment and a 3-year management plan; no paid work), art. 179 (fees on approval: Law art. 251 amount, US$30 + US$30, US$25 a year, guarantee deposit) and art. 223 (renewal every two years with proof of the investment). The US$200,000 threshold was already recorded; fees, forestry route and renewal added. Other categories (pensionado, rentista, etc.) are not investment routes and are out of scope. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Immigration (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2012, 86 pp.: a new Schedule 1 of fees (visas, business staffing plans, Caymanian status, permanent residence and RERC fees by earnings band, specialist caregivers, business visitors, temporary and annual work permits, and the occupation-by-occupation annual work permit fee list pp. 26-85, out of scope; Part 3 Cayman Enterprise City CI$1,230 flat fee, out of scope). In scope: fees for the 25-year independent-means certificate (CI$500 application, CI$20,000 issue, CI$1,000 dependant, CI$500 variation), the Certificate of Direct Investment (CI$1,000, CI$20,000, CI$1,000 per dependant, CI$500 variation, CI$1,000 per dependant annual plus work-permit-equivalent annual fee), the business presence certificate (CI$1,000, CI$5,000, CI$1,000 per dependant, CI$500 variation, annual work-permit-equivalent fee) and CI$50 duplicates (business presence, direct investment, permanent independent means). The schedule has no issue or application fee for the permanent independent-means certificate itself. Added: 13 terms and 1 event; the three issue fees were already recorded (t-e02df43ec4, t-00a8b87354, t-5d2f75c0da). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Immigration (Amendment) (No. 4) Regulations 2017, 5 pp.: reg 14 (25-year independent-means certificate): Grand Cayman CI$120,000 annual income or CI$400,000 deposit, plus CI$1m invested of which CI$500,000 in developed real estate; Sister Islands CI$75,000 income or CI$400,000 deposit, plus CI$500,000 of which CI$250,000 in real estate; definition of assets. Reg 14B: permanent certificate CI$2m (was CI$1.6m). Reg 14C: new business presence categories (hedge fund incubation; Cayman Brac back-office; exempted companies) and senior management thresholds (work permit fee CI$20,925, or CI$5,000 for the Cayman Brac category). Schedule 1: "per dependant" inserted and CI$1,000 per dependant p.a. fees for the three certificates. Made 17 May 2017, gazetted 26 May 2017. Added: 9 terms and 2 events; CI$1m and CI$2m terms and event e-45f0a5efc5 were already recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Immigration Regulations (2014 Revision), 128 pp. Out of scope: work permit procedures, visas, points system for permanent residence (Schedule 2), business staffing plans, the occupation fee list (pp. 34-91) and forms for other certificates. In scope: reg 14 (25-year independent-means certificate: CI$120,000 income AND CI$500,000 invested of which CI$250,000 real estate on Grand Cayman; CI$75,000 and CI$250,000/CI$125,000 on the Sister Islands); reg 14A Certificate of Direct Investment CI$1m; reg 14B permanent certificate CI$1.6m and quota 250 a year; reg 14C business presence (physical premises, four full-time resident employees, approved categories, senior management at a CI$20,925 work permit fee); Schedule 1 fees for the three certificates and the permanent certificate (CI$500 application, CI$100,000 issue, CI$1,000 per dependant, CI$500 variation) and CI$50 duplicates; Form 3 (25-year certificate). Added: 10 terms; four terms from this source already existed (t-0684e733b5, t-4604d5c722, t-337f4426f1, t-aaf25e822e). Fees equal to the 2012 schedule are recorded once, from cym-imm-amend2-regs-2012. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Immigration Regulations (2018 Revision), 128 pp.: consolidation to February 2018 including the 2017 amendments. Investor provisions (reg 14, 14A, 14B incl. quota 250, 14C; Schedule 1 fees pp. 32-35; Form 3) are word-for-word the 2017 amended text and the 2014 fee amounts, already recorded from cym-imm-amend4-regs-2017, cym-imm-regs-2014rev and cym-imm-amend2-regs-2012; the notes of those terms say the 2018 revision is unchanged. Rest (work permits, visas, points system, occupation fees) out of scope. No new rows: nothing in it differs from the earlier sources. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Immigration (Transition) Bill 2018, 87 pp.: memorandum (WORC and Customs and Border Control from 1 Jan 2019; financial standing to be shown by declarations from licensed professionals for the investor certificates; business presence criteria to be revised); Parts on WORC, Boards, appeals (refusals of investor certificates appealable to the Caymanian Status and Permanent Residency Board), Caymanian status, permanent residence (s.37(12) annual declaration for s.41/42 holders), s.41-46 independent-means certificates (25 years, age 18, 30 days a year, quota gazetted by Cabinet, revocation), s.47-48 Certificate of Direct Investment (6-month approval in principle, 25 years, audited accounts in years 2 and 5, 90 days a year), s.50 business presence (same as 2012 Law), work permits and regulations (out of scope). The Bill sets no amounts (they are "prescribed"). Added: 5 terms and 1 event; event e-112d2118b5 already recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

European Commission press release IP/22/2068 (6 Apr 2022): reasoned opinion to Malta; Cyprus paragraph says Cyprus stopped processing applications and as of 15 Oct 2021 revoked the citizenship of 39 investors (row and event already recorded); Bulgaria's parliament approved ending its scheme on 24 Mar 2022 (Bulgaria's final vote is already an event, dated 2022-03 from another source); Malta's original scheme near its cap of 1,800 successful main applicants (cap already recorded for Malta from other sources) and suspension for Russian/Belarusian nationals on 2 Mar 2022 (already an event). Nothing further to add. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Regulations ΚΔΠ 379/2020 (gazette 18 Aug 2020, 14 pp.): honorary naturalisation categories; investor criteria (two EUR 100,000 contributions, waiver for EUR 400,000 priority-sector business investment, EUR 2m investment in real estate/development, business with 9 Cypriot/EU employees, AIFs (max EUR 200,000 in new CSE shares) or financial assets, combinations; EUR 500,000 residence for life; EUR 2.5m if resale homes; executives with EUR 100,000 tax over 3 years; 5-year holding and annual reporting); additional conditions (clean record, PEP/sanctions/Interpol bans, Schengen visa, 6-month residence permit); family members, parents' EUR 500,000 home or EUR 1m joint home; Supervisory Committee, provider register (annual renewal), Control Unit, provider duties, fines up to EUR 350,000/700,000; advertising annex. No statistics. Four terms already recorded; six terms and one event added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Ministry of Interior statement (9 Nov 2023) agreeing with the Audit Office's findings on the fast-track residence programme (examples up to October 2022) and listing the May 2023 tightening (annual proof of investment and income, clean criminal record every three years, funds from the applicant's or spouse's own account) and stepped-up checks. No numbers. The rule changes are already recorded as the 2023-04-21 event and the 2023 criteria terms (from cyp-moi-rp-criteria-2023 and cyp-crmd-rp-criteria-2023); the audit report's publication is the 2023-11-09 event. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Ministry of Interior / Land Registry release (28 Apr 2023): revised fast-track residence criteria approved 21 Apr 2023, in force 2 May 2023; previous scheme let one EUR 300,000 property cover parents and in-laws, now not; annual proof of investment and income; applicants who filed sale contracts with the Land Registry 2 Jan-28 Apr 2023 may apply under the criteria in force since 24 Mar 2021. Event and the EUR 300,000 term already recorded; no statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Budget address for FY2023/24 (49 pages, July 2023, "National Reset"): growth and fiscal outturn FY2022/23, recurrent and capital estimates by ministry (tables pp. 10-12), housing (344 homes under construction, 327 more planned; financing not stated as CBI), health, education, airport, agriculture, tourism, small business loans, revenue estimates (Table 1 p. 40: non-tax revenue EC$645.5m budget 2023/24 and EC$649.3m forecast 2022/23, no separate CBI line), revenue measures. Programme content: hotels built under the CBI programme created "hundreds of jobs" (p. 36, no number); Debt Repayment Fund established April 2023 and US$5,000 levy per CBI investor from 1 September 2023 (p. 45; levy term and event already recorded, fund event added); new annual licence fees for non-resident CBI agents (US$15,000) and promoters (US$10,000) from 1 October 2023 (p. 45; terms and event added). No CBI revenue figure is printed separately. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Budget address for FY2026/27 (41 pages, July 2026): revenue estimates (p. 7: tax EC$473.53m, non-tax EC$558.57m; no separate CBI line), recurrent expenditure by ministry and economic classification (Tables 1-3, image tables, OCR checked; no CBI line), EC$75.2m for CBI marketing and due-diligence services in the Ministry of Finance allocation (p. 9, recorded), a section on the CBI programme (pp. 19-21: what CBI financed after Hurricane Maria, real-estate route financing hotels and ecolodges, EU visa-suspension pressure; no programme numbers), population policy incl. citizenship through a grandparent (not CBI) and CBI long-term engagement under the ECCIRA Act (pp. 32-33: 30 days physical presence in the first five years, recorded as a term; Act passage event already recorded), Vulnerability Risk and Resilience Fund at EC$28.3m on 30 June 2026 (p. 34, not described here as CBI-financed, not recorded), tax measures. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IMF Country Report, 2018 Article IV consultation for Dominica (69 pages, September 2018, after Hurricane Maria): staff report, text tables, Tables 1-3b, DSA, external assessment annex, statements. Programme content: description of the CBI (US$100,000 contribution or US$200,000 real estate; term already recorded); CBI revenue and balances excluding CBI in EC$ and % of GDP FY2012/13-FY2023/24 (Tables 3a/3b, pp. 35-36: all columns recorded; CBI revenue FY2012/13-FY2018/19 was already recorded); "Recent Fiscal Developments" text table (p. 10) with CBI revenue and overall balance excl. CBI for July-February and July-September / October-February of FY2016/17 and FY2017/18, and the nominal change of CBI revenue (recorded; full-year columns duplicate Table 3b; a new change indicator proposed); macro outlook text table (p. 11) repeating the overall balance excl. CBI (recorded once); average deficit excl. CBI 2018-21 and CBI path to near 2.5% of GDP (p. 12, recorded); chart of CBI inflows and grants (p. 12) and Figure p. 31 without printed CBI values; underlying primary balance anchor (excludes CBI, grants and transitory investment together; not recorded); AID Bank credit lines of 0.3% of GDP funded with CDB loans and CBI resources (p. 21, mixed funding, not recorded); DSA with sudden stop in CBI in FY2019/20 (pp. 42-51, debt ratios only); BOP capital transfers "Other" include ECP inflows (p. 34, not CBI-only); Annex II CBI revenue 20.3% of GDP in 2017 and 1% steady state (p. 53, recorded); events (Erika, Maria) already recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IMF Country Report, 2021 Article IV consultation for Dominica (79 pages, published February 2022): staff report, text tables, Tables 1-2b, BOP, external sector assessment, debt sustainability analysis, Executive Director statement. Programme content: CBI revenue and balances excluding CBI (with and without natural-disaster cost) in EC$ and % of GDP FY2016/17-FY2026/27 (Tables 2a/2b pp. 34-35, all columns recorded; several CBI revenue values were already recorded); Table 1 (pp. 5, 33) primary balance excluding CBI, identical except FY2016/17 (-19.6 vs -2.7; both recorded, conflict flagged); p. 10 and p. 25/41 "29.5" and "30 percent of GDP" CBI revenue in FY2020/21 (rounded repeats, not recorded again); p. 15 macro text table repeating overall balance excl. CBI (recorded once); DSA text table 3 (p. 60) CBI revenue 2020-2025 in the 2020 and 2021 Article IV (recorded; the 2021 column differs from Table 2b for 2022-2025); CBI revenue +145% in FY2020/21 and tapering to 14% of GDP by 2026 (p. 59; the 145% recorded, the 14% equals Table 2b); external annex: CBI 24.5% of GDP (2021 on p. 42, 2020 on p. 43, conflicting) and average 22.1% 2016-2021 (recorded); policy advice on allocating CBI revenue to the Vulnerability and Resilience Fund and debt service (staff calibration of 12% of deposits plus 1.5% of GDP a year, illustrative reallocation of 2% and 1.5% of GDP: recommendations, not recorded); BOP note on errors and omissions from CBI recording timing; government deposits (11% of GDP) accumulated mainly from CBI (p. 70, not a CBI account figure; not recorded); charts without printed CBI values (pp. 14, 30-31); new international airport financed with CBI revenue at an estimated cost of 65% of GDP (pp. 6, 14; recorded under a proposed indicator). No rules or events beyond those already recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

IMF Country Report, 2025 Article IV consultation for Dominica (93 pages): press release, staff report, Tables 1-5, external assessment, past-advice annex, consolidation-scenario annex, data annex, DSA. Programme content: Table 3a CBI revenue EC$ and US$ FY2020/21-FY2030/31 and Table 3b CBI revenue and primary/overall balance excluding CBI in % of GDP (all columns now recorded; columns unmarked = actual, 2024 'Est.' = estimate, later = projection; Table 1 repeats the primary balance excl. CBI and marks 2024 'Prel.'); Table 2 BOP CBI inflows US$ and % of GDP 2020-2030 (all recorded; Table 1 and the Table 3b memorandum 'Citizenship By Investment' line repeat the same calendar-year % series, recorded once); macro text table p. 11 and Annex IV scenario table p. 48 overall balance excl. CBI (scenario recorded with category=imf_consolidation_scenario; it prints the same values as the baseline); DSA Table 3 p. 71 CBI revenue in the 2024 Article IV (recorded as earlier vintage); VRF balance 1.0% of GDP March 2025, VRF target 12% at 1.5% a year, DRF target 1.3%, VRF 12% by 2032 under scenario 2 vs 1% baseline (recorded). Not recorded: rounded or bounded statements (CBI 'above 11.8 percent of GDP' since Maria, 'around 30 percent' 2021-24, '15¾ percent' = Table 3b), DSA Table 4 'use of government deposits from excess CBI' (deposit flows, not CBI amounts), fiscal measures table (CBI due diligence excluded, no amount), charts without printed values (pp. 10, 14, 29-30, image pages OCR-checked), governance narrative (FIU due diligence unit, Six Principles, agent rules, passport recall; no dates or numbers beyond events already recorded). Note: existing rows from this report (FY2020/21 and FY2024/25 CBI revenue, 2020 inflows) carry status estimate/provisional set before the 'unmarked column = actual' rule; FY2020/21 should arguably be actual. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

OECS media release (June 2024) on implementing the CBI Memorandum of Agreement: signatories, MOA published March 2024, US$200,000 minimum price from 1 July 2024 and ban on discounting (already recorded as term and events), interim 7-member regulatory commission pending a regional regulator and its functions (event added). No other numbers. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Citizenship by Investment Regulations 2024 (S.R.O. 1 of 2024, 35 pages, gazetted 25 January 2024): definitions (dependants incl. students up to 30), application procedure, monthly information sharing with JRCC, denial and deprivation grounds, real-estate resale (3 years) and reuse (5 years) limits, enhanced due diligence for specified countries (US$25,000/15,000/15,000/10,000), interviews, agents and promoters (eligibility, fees US$20,000 plus renewal US$15,500 / US$15,000, 10% late penalty), promotional restrictions (Schedule 2), Schedule 1 fees and contributions (government fees on the real-estate route, fund contributions by family size, due diligence, interview and processing fees, post-citizenship additions, certificate fee). All amounts recorded as terms (the US$100,000 contribution and US$200,000 real-estate minimum were already recorded); the regulations event already exists. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations 2017 (S.R.O. 23 of 2017, 3 pages): 12-month schedule from 1 September 2017 with lower government fees on the real-estate route by family size, fund contributions by family size, due diligence fees and child registration fee. All amounts recorded as terms (main-applicant government fee and US$100,000 contribution were already recorded); event already exists. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Citizenship by Investment Regulations 2014 (S.R.O. 37 of 2014, 16 pages): definitions, establishment of the CBI Unit, application rules, denial grounds, real-estate resale (3 years) and reuse (5 years) limits, notification within three months, promotion rules (fine up to $1,000, not recorded), review committee, repeal of the 2013 regulations, Schedule of fees and contributions (agent US$5,000, promoter US$2,000 a year, government fees on the real-estate route, fund contributions by family size, due diligence fees, child registration fee, post-citizenship additions) and agent duties. All amounts recorded as terms (US$100,000 contribution and US$200,000 real-estate minimum were already recorded); the regulations event already exists. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).
